title: Morrow: reviewed company memory for AI agents
excerpt: Morrow gives AI agents one reviewed answer to questions about how a company works. It reads Slack, Linear, GitHub, Notion, call transcripts and support tickets, finds where they contradict each other and asks the team that owns the topic which version is right. Agents get only approved answers, each with the sources behind it.
challenge: A company's rules live in Slack threads, calls, tickets, docs and pull requests, and these sources drift apart. One thread says priority accounts get a reply within four hours. The terms in Notion still say next business day. An agent that searches finds both. It then asks a person or passes one version on as fact. Nobody owns the answer, and nobody knows which sources are out of date.
solution: Morrow connects to six kinds of source: Slack, Linear, GitHub, Notion, call transcripts and support tickets. It reads them and links every decision to the message, document or commit it came from. Each source carries the time of its last sync, so Morrow can tell when a claim is stale. Morrow then flags sources that contradict each other, rules that are out of date and topics that nobody owns. Each one becomes a review task with the evidence attached. The team that owns the topic, for example Ops or Security, picks the right version and approves it. Until then, an agent that asks about the topic gets no answer and is sent to that team. An approved answer becomes a skill file that tells an agent when to use the answer and what evidence it needs. Agents fetch answers and skill files through an API or as an MCP tool, and every response states its review status and its sources. If an agent asks a question that has no reviewed answer, Morrow adds it to the review queue. An audit trail records who approved or changed what.
